newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's economy grows five pct this year - official.
newsitem.headline: Iran's economy grows five pct this year - official.

text.p: Iran's economy grew five percent and its hard currency reserves expanded by $2.5 billion in the current Iranian year to March 20, 1997, the Central Bank governor was quoted as saying on Thursday.
"The governor of the Central Bank of Iran said...that Iran's gross domestic product (GDP) increased by five percent during the current Iranian year," the official news agency IRNA said.
It said Central Bank Governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh was speaking on a visit to Tokyo on Wednesday. IRNA did not specify if it was referring to nominal or real growth.
Official figures show that annual GDP growth averaged six percent from 1989/90 to 1995/96.
Nourbakhsh put Iran's trade surplus in the current year at $5 billion compared to $5.7 billion the previous year.
He said the country had met all its foreign debt payments on time in the current year and had boosted its hard currency reserves by $2.5 billion.
Last year Iranian reserves stood at $3.65 billion.
Iran's foreign debt soared to more than $30 billion by the early 1990s caused by lax control over an explosive import bill after the end of its eight-year war with Iraq in 1988.

Latest Central Bank figures show the country's rescheduled repayment obligations at $7.15 billion in 1997/98, $4.19 billion in 1998/99, falling to $2.62 billion in 1999/2000 and just $637 million in 2000/2001.
